issues.where: section: The formula has the three properties
issues.problem: The cancellation proof of the alternating property relied on 'composing sigma with a transposition changes its sign', which was used without proof and without saying so (the transpose-invariance remark is fine). The lesson defines sgn by counting inversions, so this is exactly the missing step.
issues.fix: Added a short complete proof: when the values in positions k<l are exchanged, the pair (k,l) changes status, each position m between them changes both pairs (k,m),(m,l) or neither, and positions outside exchange the statuses of their pairs with k and l, so the inversion count changes by an odd number. Verified pair by pair over all permutations of 6.

issues.problem: Cofactor expansion was justified only by 'grouping the Leibniz terms', which leaves the (-1)^{i+j} sign unproved and does not say so; later solutions (Vandermonde) use expansion along a row and the chessboard sign.
issues.fix: Now says explicitly that the sign bookkeeping is omitted, and that the expansion also works along any column. Added an exact check of expansion along every row and column.

issues.problem: Characterised det as the unique function that 'changes sign when two columns are swapped', while the lesson's uniqueness theorem uses 'vanishes when two columns are equal'. Over R or C these are equivalent, but the card should match the theorem.
issues.fix: Card now says 'zero whenever two columns are equal'.

issues.problem: Cramer's rule stated without the hypothesis that A is invertible; paragraph was also padded.
issues.fix: Added 'For invertible A'; tightened the paragraph (same links).

issues.problem: Closing remark wordy.
issues.fix: Shortened.

issues.problem: Length is long; trimmed only padding.
issues.fix: minutes 18 -> 17.

issues.problem: Said the stationary distribution of a Markov chain (and the other listed quantities) 'are all eigenvalues'; a stationary distribution is an eigenvector, not an eigenvalue, and vibration frequencies are square roots of eigenvalues of the governing matrix.
issues.fix: Now says these are all read off from eigenvalues and eigenvectors.

issues.problem: 'The stationary distribution of a Markov chain is an eigenvector for the eigenvalue 1' is false for the transition matrix P with the usual row-stochastic convention: it is a left eigenvector (eigenvector of P^T). The entry link already said 'left'.
issues.fix: Now says left eigenvector of the transition matrix (an eigenvector of its transpose).

issues.problem: The field was not fixed: 'real or complex entries' and 'a number lambda' left unclear whether a real matrix can have a complex eigenvalue and where v lives, so 'the eigenvalues are the roots of p_A' was ambiguous (the rotation example has no real eigenvalues but complex ones).
issues.fix: Definition now fixes F = R or C with lambda in F and v in F^n, notes a real matrix may be viewed over C with extra non-real eigenvalues; 'roots in F are the eigenvalues over F'. Card summary and key 3 now say eigenvalues are taken in C with algebraic multiplicity.

issues.problem: 'AB and BA have the same characteristic polynomial' was stated without proof without saying so.
issues.fix: Marked as a standard fact not proved here (statement correct for square matrices; checked on random matrices). Added the eigenspace dimensions in the counterexample.

issues.problem: 'For symmetric matrices the eigenvectors can be chosen perpendicular' omits 'real' (false for complex symmetric matrices); 'mysteriously match the zeros of the zeta function' is hype and imprecise.
issues.fix: 'real symmetric'; zeta sentence rewritten as a comparison of spacing statistics.

issues.problem: 'signs of the real parts decide stability' is imprecise (zero real parts are not decided by signs).
issues.fix: Now: every solution tends to 0 exactly when every eigenvalue has negative real part.

issues.problem: Vague closing sentence about olympiad problems.
issues.fix: Removed.

issues.where: proof of the multiplicity criterion, part 1
issues.problem: Claimed 'the determinant of a block triangular matrix is the product of the determinants of the diagonal blocks (expand repeatedly along the first column)'. The parenthetical justification is wrong for a general block triangular matrix; it only works here because the top-left block of tI - P^{-1}AP is (t-lambda)I_g. The use of similarity invariance of p_A was also implicit.
issues.fix: Rewritten to use the actual shape: similar matrices have the same characteristic polynomial, and expanding g times along the first column of tI - P^{-1}AP gives (t-lambda)^g p_E(t).

issues.problem: The theorem used F^n but F was never introduced, and the definition did not say over which field P and D live, although the lesson then distinguishes diagonalisability over R and over C.
issues.fix: Definition now fixes F = R or C and requires P, D with entries in F ('diagonalisable over F').

issues.problem: 'A^k x lines up with p_1 and has size about |lambda_1|^k' is loose (only the direction converges to the line through p_1; the size is |lambda_1|^k up to a constant).
issues.fix: Reworded precisely.

issues.problem: The criterion was given only over C; the card's 'the obstruction is an eigenvalue whose eigenspace is smaller than its multiplicity' is false over R (rotations).
issues.fix: Card says 'over C the only obstruction ...'; pitfall adds the real criterion (all eigenvalues real and g = a). Added checks.

issues.problem: Description of Jordan form ('diagonal blocks with 1s just above the diagonal, one block per independent eigenvector') was garbled.
issues.fix: Rewritten: block diagonal, each block with a single eigenvalue on the diagonal and 1s just above, as many blocks as the maximal number of independent eigenvectors.

issues.problem: 'Covariance is an inner product on random variables with mean zero' is false as stated: it needs finite variance, and positivity fails unless variables equal almost surely are identified.
issues.fix: Both now say: on mean-zero random variables with finite variance, identifying variables equal with probability 1.

issues.problem: 'A symmetric matrix has an orthonormal basis of eigenvectors' omits 'real'; 'Gram-Schmidt ... is the standard numerically stable way' overstates (classical Gram-Schmidt is not numerically stable; stable QR uses other algorithms).
issues.fix: 'real symmetric'; QR described as a standard tool when computed in a numerically stable way.

issues.problem: 'differs from the tangent line or the chord' was vague (which tangent line?).
issues.fix: Now: neither the chord y = x nor any tangent line of y = x^2 (checked).

issues.where: entry.sum / section: Angles and orthonormal bases
issues.problem: 'linear' without saying in which argument over C; 'Rotations and reflections are the examples' suggests these are all orthogonal matrices.
issues.fix: 'linear in the first argument, conjugate-symmetric over C'; 'are examples'.

issues.problem: Checked the m <= n+1 proof line by line (independence of v_1..v_{m-1} via the positive/negative split and pairing with v_m) and the regular-simplex construction: correct. No change.
issues.fix: Added independent checks (norms n/(n+1), cosine -1/n, 120 degrees for n=2; the key inner-product identity).

issues.problem: The complex picture stopped at Hermitian matrices; the precise statement for unitary diagonalisability (normal matrices, with complex D) was missing, so a reader could think Hermitian is the exact condition for unitary diagonalisation.
issues.fix: Added: a complex matrix is unitarily diagonalisable (D possibly non-real) iff it is normal, stated as not proved here; Hermitian, real orthogonal and unitary matrices are normal. Added check.

issues.problem: Quantum observables listed among 'symmetric matrices' although they are Hermitian.
issues.fix: 'Symmetric and Hermitian matrices'.

issues.problem: Real-eigenvalue argument, invariance of q_1-perp, symmetry of the restricted matrix, conic, Rayleigh example and A^k = I example all checked and correct.
issues.fix: Added independent checks (conic semi-axes and area, SOS identities, normal vs non-normal).

issues.problem: The Frobenius-norm optimality was asserted only in passing inside the proof block, and the card claimed the truncated SVD is 'the best low-rank approximation' without saying in which norm (it is not optimal for every norm, as the lesson's own pitfall notes) or that the minimiser need not be unique.
issues.fix: Theorem now states both inequalities exactly with the truncated SVD A_k (0 <= k < min(m,n), A_k = A for k >= r) and the Frobenius error (sum_{i>k} sigma_i^2)^{1/2}; the proof says the Frobenius inequality is omitted and how its equality case follows from exercise 3. Card: 'a best approximation of rank at most k in the operator and Frobenius norms'. Key 3 now gives the range of k.

issues.problem: Polar decomposition described as 'a rotation times a positive semidefinite stretch'; UV^T can be a reflection.
issues.fix: 'an orthogonal matrix (a rotation, possibly combined with a reflection) times a symmetric positive semidefinite stretch'. Added check.

issues.problem: Field hypothesis: the lesson works over C only and never says what happens over other fields; the connection said rational canonical form replaces Jordan form 'over fields where polynomials need not split, such as finite fields', which wrongly suggests Jordan form never exists there.
